title: fix(runtime): the resume door checks WHO is resuming — the run's starter, or the sys_automation_run read grant (#19987)
body:
Fixes #19987

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`POST /automation/:name/runs/:runId/resume` now checks WHO is resuming. Before, the arm validated the body and called `automationService.resume(runId, signal)` without reading any identity. So an authenticated caller holding another user's run id (`u2` on a run whose `getRun().trigger.userId` is `u1`) got `200` and `resume` ran. The resumed run then continued under the context STORED on the run (`engine.ts` `const context = run.context`): its data nodes ran as `u1`, with values `u2` submitted. The screen read on the same pause already refused `u2`.

The write door now asks the screen read's question (maintainer ruling Option B on #7968, applied to the write by triage's direction `5817076635`). Both doors call one predicate, `isRunStarterOrRunStateReader` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`):

- the caller is the run's own starter (`getRun(runId).trigger.userId`), OR
- the caller holds read access to `sys_automation_run` (the operator override, asked through `mayReadRunState`, the #7900 question), OR
- the caller is a system context.

Everyone else gets `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, the read twin's code and status, and `resume()` is never called, so the pause stays parked. `refuseUnrelatedScreenRead` and the new `refuseUnrelatedResume` are now two thin guard clauses over that one predicate. Each owns only its refusal sentence and WHERE it asks. The read twin's behaviour and message are byte-identical to before.

## `resumeAuthority` today, as the ruling asks (read first, per triage's binding limit)

`resumeAuthority` is the closed enum `'any' | 'service'` (`packages/spec/src/automation/node-executor.zod.ts`). It names no person. Measured on `origin/main` `6bf7f1c0`:

| Node type | Declared `resumeAuthority` | Where | On this REST door |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `screen` | `'any'` | `service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts` | the route is the intended door; "any" names no specific caller ⇒ the new gate applies |
| `wait` | `'any'` | `service-automation/src/builtin/wait-node.ts` | same |
| `map` | `'any'` | `service-automation/src/builtin/map-node.ts` | same (the engine still walks to a service-gated item) |
| `subflow` | `'any'` | `service-automation/src/builtin/subflow-node.ts` | same (the engine still judges the child the signal lands on) |
| `approval` | `'service'` | `plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts` | refused by the ENGINE for every caller: the service marker is a symbol no JSON body can carry |
| `approval_revise` | `'service'` | `plugin-approvals/src/approval-revise-node.ts` | same |
| any undeclared type | treated as `'service'` (#5561) | `engine.ts` `resolveResumeAuthority` | same |

An approver decides through `ApprovalService`, which resumes in process (`approval-service.ts`: `this.automation!.resume!(runId, { ...signal, [RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE]: true })`) and never enters `handleAutomationRequest`. So no caller this door admitted before is a caller the node names, and triage's limit 「不得拒绝节点自身 `resumeAuthority` 已经明确授权的人」 holds by measurement: the set of node-named callers on this door is empty. The node gate still answers, unchanged and word for word, behind the new gate (pinned: an admitted starter on an `approval` pause still gets the engine's own 403 message).

## The two doors' rules, side by side

| | REST `POST /automation/:name/runs/:runId/resume` (this PR) | MCP `resume_run` (`mcp.ts` `resumeActionRun`, unchanged) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Run's own starter | admitted | admitted |
| `sys_automation_run` read grant, not the starter | admitted (operator override, as on the screen read) | refused (starter-only by design, no operator override) |
| System context | admitted | n/a |
| Stranger | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | `404` (one not-found for unknown, finished and foreign runs) |
| Node gate (`resumeAuthority`) | still applies behind this gate | still applies |
| Engine answer classification | `classifyResumeResult` | `classifyResumeResult` (same table) |

## Order of operations, decided by measurement

The gate runs AFTER the body checks and immediately BEFORE `resume()`.

- **After the body checks.** They read nothing about the run, so every `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` is byte-identical for every caller. The gate's lookup is spent only on a request the engine would otherwise receive.
- **Before `resume()`.** A refused resume consumes nothing.
- **Fail-closed on a run `getRun` cannot resolve. There is no 404-first step, and this is where the write departs from the read twin.** The read twin answers 404 first because `getSuspendedScreen` is an authoritative "is there anything to disclose" check. The write has no such probe short of `resume()`, and `resume()` consumes the pause. `getRun`'s `null` is not authoritative. The engine returns `null` for a run that is parked and resumable when the durable read degrades (`engine.ts` `getRun`: "a run that is parked and resumable reports as if it had never run"). It also returns `null` after the 1000-entry in-memory ring evicts the entry on a deployment with no suspended-run store (`DEFAULT_MAX_EXECUTION_LOG_SIZE`, the `splice` in `recordLog`), and a caller who can start runs can cause that eviction. Letting `null` through would open the gate in exactly those states.
- **What moves, and for whom.** Only for a caller who is neither the run's starter, nor a grant holder, nor a system context: an unknown or finished run now answers them this `403` instead of the engine's `404`. As a side effect, a stranger can no longer tell a paused run id from an unknown one here. For every caller the gate admits, every engine answer is unchanged, including the `404` for unknown and finished runs (both pinned). One cost falls on honest callers: a caller WITHOUT the grant who mistypes a run id now gets `403` rather than `404`.

## Tests

All readings are on HEAD `b4cb8a4d`, unless a line says otherwise.

- **Failing probe first** (the card's named probe, committed as a test). `automation-resume-caller-gate.test.ts` was run against the unfixed arm (base `6bf7f1c0`) and gave `Tests 17 failed | 33 passed (50)`. The stranger `u2` on `u1`'s run got `200`, with `resume` called.
- **New suite** `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-resume-caller-gate.test.ts`: 50 cases. Every refusal row asserts the envelope `code` AND `status`, and asserts that `resume` was NOT called:
  - stranger refused, with the exact message, and nothing about the caller's authorization topology in the refusal (#7450);
  - a run with no `trigger.userId` refused;
  - a run `getRun` cannot resolve refused;
  - a `getRun` throw refused, even for the starter;
  - a service with no `getRun`: refused unless the grant admits;
  - permission subsystem down: stranger refused, starter admitted;
  - starter admitted with NO grant: the over-block guard; the signal is forwarded field by field and `explain` is never called;
  - grant holder admitted: `explain` is asked for `read` on `sys_automation_run` with the caller's own context;
  - system context admitted without asking anything;
  - the node gate's own 403 still arrives word for word for an admitted starter;
  - unchanged answers: starter on a finished run gets the engine's 404; grant holder on an unknown id gets the engine's 404; a malformed body is refused `VALIDATION_FAILED` before the gate for every caller; anonymous gets `401` first; no security service, or a partial one, admits;
  - a parity table (3 callers × 5 security postures × 2 runs = 30 cases) that drives BOTH doors with the same inputs and requires the same verdict, and on refusal the same `code`, the same `status` and the same requirement sentence.
- **Rewritten pin.** `automation-screen-read-gate.test.ts` had a case pinning the defect itself ("leaves `resume`'s own authority checks alone": stranger not 403, `resume` called). It is replaced by two cases: the same stranger is refused at `resume` (same code and status, `resume` not called), and the triggering user is admitted with no grant. Comments in three sibling suites that said the resume door had no route-level gate are corrected. Their assertions are unchanged and still green.
- **Mutation leg** (`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, on committed `a99d03a4`, the gate's code identical at HEAD). It replaced `if (unrelated) return unrelated;` with an inert statement: anchor 1 → 0, blob `467c4019f123` → `e8f9a4915391`. With the gate removed, the two gate suites went `Tests 15 failed | 57 passed (72)`: every stranger and unresolved row turned red, and every starter, grant and system row stayed green. The direction is red, as expected. Restore: blob == HEAD (`467c4019f123`) and `git diff HEAD` empty. The suite imports the arm by relative source path, so no `dist/` is involved.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2` (on `a99d03a4`; the later commit changes only a ledger note string and a docs table row): `Test Files 276 passed (276)`, `Tests 3893 passed | 1 skipped`.
- On HEAD `b4cb8a4d`, the nine suites that read the route ledger or drive the resume arm (`route-ledger.conformance`, `http-dispatcher`, `discovery-schema-conformance`, `auth-forward-fault-sanitization` and the five automation gate suites) were re-run: `Test Files 9 passed (9)`, `Tests 436 passed (436)`.
- `--project repo`: `Test Files 2 passed`, `Tests 69 passed`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0. Output: `check:test-typecheck: OK — @objectstack/runtime's test layer compiles`, and the new suite is not in the debt ledger.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/flow-durable-suspend.dogfood.test.ts` against the rebuilt runtime `dist/` (it carries `isRunStarterOrRunStateReader`): `Tests 11 passed (11)`. That includes the real-engine resume after a real cold boot.
- **Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on HEAD derives 92 commands. All 92 were run with exit codes captured before any pipe, and all exited 0. `--ran` reconciliation: `92 derived, 92 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` ("a DERIVED zero — all 92 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3"). Two runs needed a prerequisite first. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` refused with exit 3 (no `dist/`), and `check:skill-examples` refused the same way (no client-react `.d.ts`). A full `turbo run build` then ran (`73 successful, 73 total`), and all three were re-run green before the final union.
- **Roster gates** whose rosters sit under a touched directory: `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check:route-ledger-census`, and also `check:error-status-conformance`. All exit 0.
- `pnpm lint` (the full union, `eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0 in 112s.

Two gates were red on the first pass, and both reds were caused by this diff:

- `check:system-context-census`: the `isSystem` read moved from `refuseUnrelatedScreenRead` into the shared predicate. The row in `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` is re-anchored and now names the resume door.
- `check:doc-authoring`: tracker ids in the route-ledger note string. They are removed from the string.

## Docs

`content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`:

- "Who may resume" now has the caller question first and the node question second. It states the three admitted callers, the refusal, the ordering and the MCP door's stricter rule.
- The pause table's `wait` (signal) row no longer says "any caller".

## Deviations, stated rather than chosen silently

1. **Refusal sentence.** The code and status are the read twin's. The requirement clause is the read twin's, word for word: both messages are built from one constant, `PAUSED_RUN_REQUIREMENT`. The verb phrase is this door's own: "Resuming a paused run requires being the identity that triggered the run, or read access to 'sys_automation_run'." A resume refused with "Reading a paused run's screen …" would name an operation the caller did not attempt. That is the misdirection #11666 took off the toggle door. If the literal read sentence is wanted instead, it is a one-line change: `RESUME_DENY_MESSAGE = SCREEN_READ_DENY_MESSAGE`.
2. **Unknown and finished runs** keep today's answers for every caller the gate admits, not for every caller. The reasons are in "Order of operations" above.
3. **Two files beyond the claim's listed file surface.** `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`: the resume row's `note` now describes the caller gate. `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`: `check:system-context-census` refuses the tree until that row re-anchors.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- **Consequence of Option B, for the maintainer's eye.** A caller that resumes runs it did NOT start now needs `sys_automation_run` read. Examples: an integration feeding a `wait` node's signal, or support tooling. The changeset says so. No in-repo caller does this: the REST resume callers on `main` are the route mount, the client SDK method and the tests.
- `WaitExecutorConfigSchema.webhookUrlPattern` defaults to `/api/v1/automation/resume/{executionId}/{nodeId}`, a path no route serves, and it has zero runtime readers. It is dormant, not filed. Carrier: none.
- The client SDK's `automation.resume` docblock lists the resume refusals but not this 403. The list is incomplete, not wrong. Not filed. Carrier: none.

## NOT MEASURED locally (CI owns them)

- Test Core shards, Temporal Conformance, the Dogfood Regression Gate beyond the one suite above, and Dogfood Verify CLI.
- The workspace, examples and downstream type-check lanes: runtime's own `typecheck` ran. The public surface is unchanged (no export added or removed), so no importer owes a test.
- The artifact-roster, wide-population and path-scheduled CI steps that `dispatch-gates` lists outside its derived total.
